note: Authored ground truth for the role-classification holdout. Written BEFORE the rules were run against it, and the rules were not adjusted afterwards. The 10/10 on the other three sets is in-distribution — classify.ts was tuned while reading its own output on them — so this set exists to produce a number that can fail.

whyEachIsHard.weekly.md: No role word anywhere in the filename, and a date for a title. Everything is in the body: attendees, an apology, and three action items with owners.
whyEachIsHard.overview.md: A product spec wearing a decision record's clothes — an `## Decision` heading and a `**Rationale:**` paragraph, which are the two strongest signals the decisionRecord rule has. The content is requirements and scope. If the rules answer decisionRecord they have been fooled by format.
whyEachIsHard.README.md: A filename that could introduce anything, over a body that is nothing but coding conventions. The rules' filename signal offers no help and must not hurt.
whyEachIsHard.platform.md: Architecture described entirely in prose, with no heading vocabulary at all past the title — no `Components`, no `Data flow`, no `Overview`.
whyEachIsHard.checks.md: testPolicy, a role none of the other three sets contain, so nothing about it was exercised while the rules were being written.
